hero.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran deal negotiated by his own envoys
hero.body:
President Trump announced that a peace agreement with Iran "has been largely negotiated" after conversations with Pakistani mediators, Gulf allies and Israeli leadership. However, the announcement came with significant complications, as Trump's own negotiating team and Iran have presented conflicting accounts of what has actually been agreed.

Trump stated on his social media platform that "final aspects and details" of a "memorandum of understanding" remain under discussion and will be announced shortly. He claimed the Strait of Hormuz would be opened as part of the deal and indicated that an agreement had been "largely negotiated" between the United States, Iran and various other countries.

However, Iran's Fars news agency, affiliated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, rejected Trump's characterization. The agency stated that "the management of the Strait, determining the route, time, method of passage, and issuing permits will continue to be the monopoly and discretion of the Islamic Republic of Iran," directly contradicting Trump's assertions about the strait's status in any agreement. The agency said Trump's claims were "inconsistent with reality."

Multiple sources have outlined potential deal terms. According to reports, the framework would include opening the strait with no tolls during a 60-day ceasefire extension, allowing Iran to freely sell oil and initiating negotiations on its nuclear program. The United States would lift its blockade on Iranian ports in exchange. Three senior Iranian officials told the New York Times the agreement could release 25 billion dollars in frozen Iranian assets and result in nuclear negotiations within 30 to 60 days.

Trump met with his negotiating team, including special envoy Steve Witkoff and adviser Jared Kushner, to discuss the latest proposals. He also conducted calls with leaders from Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Egypt, Jordan, Bahrain, Pakistan and Turkey.

The uncertainty surrounding the deal has drawn criticism from Republican hawks. Mike Pompeo, who served as CIA director and secretary of state during Trump's first term, denounced the reported terms as too similar to the 2015 nuclear deal negotiated by the Obama administration, which Trump withdrew from in 2018.

However, Robert Malley, one of Obama's negotiators, responded that while the approach differed from what his team would have taken, he would accept the current deal if it ended the war, stopped loss of life and prevented economic damage.

Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif later said Pakistan hopes to host another round of talks between the United States and Iran "very soon," describing recent diplomatic calls as "very useful and productive."

The negotiations remain fluid with no confirmed timeline for finalization. Trump has threatened to resume striking Iran if a deal meeting American demands is not reached.

cards.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes at Florida launch site, halting national security missions
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on the launchpad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida on Thursday night during a static fire test, destroying the launch facility and raising serious questions about NASA's timeline for returning humans to the moon.

The explosion occurred at 9pm ET at Launch Complex 36, creating a massive fireball visible from miles away. An orange sky was reported in Fort Pierce, 185 kilometers to the south, and shockwaves were felt by residents across Florida's space coast and even in South Carolina hundreds of miles north. Flames continued burning at the launchpad for more than two hours after the incident.

Blue Origin described the event as an "anomaly" and confirmed that all employees were safe and uninjured. Company founder Jeff Bezos acknowledged the setback on social media, stating "It's too early to know the root cause but we're already working to find it. Very rough day, but we'll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying. It's worth it."

The timing of the explosion is particularly significant for NASA's ambitions. The agency had announced just the day before that Blue Origin won a contract to launch the first of three planned missions to begin construction of a 20 billion dollar lunar base. The New Glenn rocket is intended to carry landers to the moon as part of NASA's broader effort to establish a permanent lunar presence and return astronauts to the surface for the first time since 1972.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman stated that the agency would conduct a full evaluation of its timeline following the explosion. "Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult," he wrote. "We will work with our partners to support a thorough investigation of this anomaly, assess near-term mission impacts, and get back to launching rockets."

The explosion marks another setback for Blue Origin as it competes with SpaceX for lucrative NASA contracts. Last month, a payload from the third flight of New Glenn ended up in the wrong orbit, and the rocket was temporarily grounded by the Federal Aviation Administration before receiving clearance to return to flight just last week. Thursday's static fire test was the first such test since that clearance.

The incident also impacts competition for upcoming missions. Blue Origin is scheduled to test its Blue Moon lander for NASA's Artemis III mission planned for 2027, competing against SpaceX's Starship Human Landing System to determine which company will ferry astronauts from orbit to the lunar surface.

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk responded to the explosion on social media, noting simply, "Rockets are hard."

cards.headline: U.S. military disables ship attempting to breach Iran blockade
cards.teaser: Central Command stopped a Gambian-flagged vessel trying to dock at an Iranian port despite multiple warnings.
cards.body:
U.S. Central Command announced that it had prevented another vessel from docking at an Iranian port amid a U.S. naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. military disabled a ship flying under a Gambian flag on Friday after the vessel did not heed numerous warnings, according to a statement from Centcom.

The action comes as the U.S. maintains a naval blockade of Iranian ports. The blockade has been a point of tension as U.S. and Iranian negotiators work toward a tentative agreement that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and extend the current ceasefire between the two nations.

cards.headline: Israeli soldiers describe ongoing killings in Gaza despite ceasefire
cards.teaser: Israeli soldiers provided rare firsthand accounts from Gaza to journalists, describing continued violence after a ceasefire agreement.
cards.body:
Israeli soldiers have provided rare firsthand accounts to journalists describing military operations continuing in Gaza after ceasefire arrangements were announced. One soldier stated that calling the situation a ceasefire "is a joke," characterizing conditions on the ground as inconsistent with official ceasefire terms.

The soldiers' testimonies reveal a gap between announced agreements and actual operations in Gaza. Their accounts offer direct perspective from personnel involved in the military operations, contrasting with official government descriptions of the security situation.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo surpasses 245 suspected deaths
cards.body:
More than 245 suspected cases of Ebola have been reported in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with confirmed deaths reaching at least 65 people, according to health officials. The outbreak is concentrated in Ituri province, a conflict-affected region that borders Uganda and South Sudan, raising concerns about potential spread across borders.

The strain identified in this outbreak is the Bundibugyo virus, detected in laboratory samples tested by the DRC's national research laboratory. This represents a significant concern because no licensed vaccine currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, unlike the more commonly seen Zaire strain of Ebola that has caused previous outbreaks in the region. Only two prior outbreaks of Bundibugyo virus have occurred, in 2007 and 2012.

The World Health Organization has estimated the death rate for this outbreak at between 30 and 50 percent based on confirmed cases. Anaïs Legand from the WHO's high threat pathogens team described this rate as "huge," meaning that up to five out of every ten infected people are likely to die.

The geographical challenges facing containment efforts are substantial. Ituri province contains numerous mining towns with constant population movement, making disease control particularly difficult. Cases have been reported mainly in the Mongwalu and Rwampara health zones, with suspected cases also appearing in the neighboring city of Bunia.

Uganda's health ministry has already confirmed cases in the country, with a 59-year-old man dying from Ebola in a Kampala hospital after traveling from the DRC. This development prompted urgent regional coordination efforts. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention convened an emergency meeting with authorities from the DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan, along with the World Health Organization and pharmaceutical companies.

Dr Jean Kaseya, director general of the Africa CDC, emphasized the importance of rapid coordination given the high population movement between affected areas and neighboring countries. According to experts, multiple factors contribute to recurring Ebola outbreaks in the region, including close human contact with animal reservoirs such as bats and possibly primates, movement between rural and urban environments, the tropical climate, and extensive rainforest coverage.

The World Health Organization's director general visited the hardest-hit areas to assess the situation and support containment efforts. Medical charities including Doctors Without Borders have deployed teams to assist health workers facing severe resource shortages and inadequate protective equipment. The organizations have described the virus's spread as deeply alarming, highlighting the significant gap between the outbreak's scale and available resources.

The DRC has experienced 16 Ebola outbreaks since the virus was first identified there in 1976, though this outbreak presents unique challenges due to the Bundibugyo strain and regional instability.

cards.headline: SoftBank commits $75 billion to build AI data centers in France
cards.teaser: The Japanese conglomerate will construct what it calls Europe's largest artificial intelligence facility.
cards.body:
SoftBank announced plans to invest up to €75 billion to build AI data centers in France, positioning the project as Europe's largest AI facility. The investment will fund the development and operation of up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity across multiple facilities dedicated to AI computing.

The commitment represents one of the largest technology infrastructure investments in Europe this year, significantly expanding the continent's artificial intelligence capabilities.

cards.headline: New car sales drop as one million American buyers leave the market
cards.teaser: Auto sales have fallen for eight consecutive months as vehicle prices strain household budgets.
cards.body:
Approximately one million buyers have exited the new car market in the United States, contributing to an eight-month decline in auto sales. The drop reflects growing financial pressure on American households as vehicle prices remain elevated.

Electric vehicle demand has collapsed alongside traditional car sales, compounding troubles for automakers. Industry analysts describe the trend as potentially long-lasting, with departed buyers unlikely to return to the market in the near term.

cards.headline: Rescuers free four men from flooded cave in Laos, two still missing
cards.teaser: Four men were freed from a flooded cave in Laos as rescue operations continue for two others still trapped inside.
cards.body:
Rescuers have freed four more men from a flooded cave system in Laos, bringing the total number of successful rescues to five. The men had been trapped for 10 days after entering the narrow tunnels on May 20 while searching for gold. Two members of the original party of seven remain missing as divers continue search efforts.

The rescue operation has proven extremely challenging, requiring teams to navigate through muddy water, sharp rocks, and narrow passages. Rescuers have been working to drain water from the cave and manage collapse hazards as they push deeper into the system to locate the two missing villagers.

cards.headline: Drone crashes into apartment building in eastern Romania
cards.teaser: A drone struck an apartment building in eastern Romania, bringing the Russia-Ukraine war directly into the lives of residents near the conflict zone.
cards.body:
Residents of an apartment building in eastern Romania experienced a loud explosion and fire when a drone crashed into their home. The incident reminded people living near the border that the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war poses direct risks to neighboring countries.

The crash prompted panic among residents as the war entered their homes in a tangible way. Romania shares a border with Ukraine and has found itself in proximity to military operations throughout the conflict.

cards.headline: Israeli soldiers describe ongoing killings in Gaza despite ceasefire
cards.teaser: Israeli soldiers provided rare firsthand accounts from Gaza to journalists, describing continued violence after a ceasefire agreement.
cards.body:
Israeli soldiers have provided rare firsthand accounts to journalists describing military operations continuing in Gaza after ceasefire arrangements were announced. One soldier stated that calling the situation a ceasefire "is a joke," characterizing conditions on the ground as inconsistent with official ceasefire terms.

The soldiers' testimonies reveal a gap between announced agreements and actual operations in Gaza. Their accounts offer direct perspective from personnel involved in the military operations, contrasting with official government descriptions of the security situation.

cards.headline: Colombia holds presidential election with leftist candidate leading polls
cards.teaser: Colombians vote in a presidential election that represents a crucial test for the political left across Latin America.
cards.body:
Colombia is holding a presidential election shadowed by resurgence of political violence. The vote represents a contest between left and right, with competing visions for addressing the country's decades-long armed conflict.

The election comes amid growing dangers for journalists covering the conflict. A 24-year-old political science student and independent journalist was killed in May while reporting on clashes between the army, paramilitaries, and dissident factions of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia in Antioquia province.

cards.headline: Edgar Morin, French intellectual and former Resistance member, dies at 104
cards.teaser: Edgar Morin, a towering figure in French intellectual life who fought in the Resistance during World War II, has died at 104.
cards.body:
Edgar Morin, known as the grandfather of French intellectuals, died at age 104 after a career that spanned multiple eras and academic disciplines. His work and public statements carried significant moral authority in France and beyond.

Morin served as a member of the French Resistance during World War II before building a distinguished career as a thinker and author. His books addressed topics across philosophy, sociology, and other fields over decades of intellectual production.

cards.headline: Ecuador accused of election interference in Colombia with tariff offer
cards.teaser: Colombia accused Ecuadorian leader Daniel Noboa of meddling in its presidential election by offering tariff concessions to a right-wing candidate.
cards.body:
Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa offered to cancel tariffs after speaking with a right-wing Colombian presidential candidate ahead of Sunday's election. The direct engagement and policy promise have drawn accusations of electoral interference from observers concerned about foreign involvement in Colombia's vote.

The election pits Colombia's leftist frontrunner against a far-right challenger, with the campaign unfolding against a backdrop of resurgent political violence. The incident has added diplomatic tensions to an already contentious race focused on competing visions for addressing Colombia's decades-long armed conflict.

cards.headline: Family of four among five killed in Virginia bus crash en route to wedding
cards.teaser: A bus driver has been charged after a crash killed five people, including a family of four traveling to a wedding.
cards.body:
A family of four died alongside one other person in a crash in Virginia, according to authorities. The family had been traveling to attend a wedding when the collision occurred.

Police charged the bus driver in connection with the crash. The incident claimed five lives total. Authorities have not released the names of the victims or detailed the circumstances that led to the collision.

cards.headline: Meteor explodes over Massachusetts, causing loud boom across New England
cards.teaser: A meteor exploded in the atmosphere over Massachusetts, causing loud noises heard throughout Southern New England.
cards.body:
A meteor traveling at 75,000 miles per hour exploded over northeastern Massachusetts and southeastern New Hampshire on Saturday afternoon, creating a blast equivalent to 300 tons of TNT. The space rock broke apart at an altitude of 40 miles, setting off sonic booms that reverberated across the region.

Residents throughout Southern New England reported hearing the loud explosions, with the impact centered around the Boston area. NASA confirmed the event occurred just after 2pm local time.

cards.headline: ICE agent wanted in Minneapolis shooting arrested in Texas
cards.teaser: An ICE agent charged in a shooting during an immigration enforcement operation in Minnesota has been captured in Texas.
cards.body:
Federal authorities arrested an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent in Texas who had been wanted in connection with a shooting in Minneapolis. The agent faced charges related to an incident that occurred during an immigration enforcement operation in January.

After evading arrest for several months, the agent was apprehended in Texas. The case has drawn attention to ICE enforcement practices and operations in the region.

cards.headline: Wife of Maine Senate candidate flagged his explicit texts to other women
cards.teaser: The wife of Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner confirmed he sent sexually explicit texts to other women during their marriage.
cards.body: Graham Platner, an oyster farmer and former U.S. Marine, exchanged sexually explicit texts with other women during his marriage, according to information his wife Amy Gertner shared with his campaign last year. Gertner said she was hurt by the public revelation of the messages. Platner is Maine's presumptive Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate and is seeking to unseat Republican Senator Susan Collins.

cards.headline: Detainees sue federal government over conditions at Texas ICE facility
cards.teaser: Immigrant detainees have filed a lawsuit accusing the federal government of inhumane treatment at a facility in El Paso, Texas.
cards.body:
A class-action lawsuit was filed against Immigration and Customs Enforcement, accusing the agency of severe human rights violations at Camp East Montana in El Paso, Texas—the largest immigration detention facility in the United States. Four detainees filed the complaint on behalf of themselves and all current and future civil detainees at the facility.

The lawsuit alleges multiple violations including inadequate medical and mental health care, inappropriate use of force, solitary confinement, unsanitary living conditions, disease outbreaks, and sexual harassment by guards. Detainees also claim they receive inadequate food. The complaint describes the overall conditions as "dire" and abusive.

cards.headline: Power outages trap elderly Cubans in high-rise buildings
cards.teaser: A 70-year-old widow in Cuba says blackouts left her and her husband trapped when he needed medical care.
cards.body:
Cuba's ongoing blackouts have created a crisis for residents living in tall buildings who rely on elevators to access their homes. A 70-year-old widow described how a power outage left her and her husband stranded when he needed urgent medical care, unable to leave their apartment because the elevator was not functioning.

The repeated outages have left high-rise residents facing constant uncertainty about whether they will be able to enter or exit their buildings. Elderly and disabled residents are particularly vulnerable, often unable to navigate stairs or leave during blackout periods.

cards.headline: SoftBank commits $75 billion to build AI data centers in France
cards.teaser: The Japanese conglomerate will construct what it calls Europe's largest artificial intelligence facility.
cards.body:
SoftBank announced plans to invest up to €75 billion to build AI data centers in France, positioning the project as Europe's largest AI facility. The investment will fund the development and operation of up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity across multiple facilities dedicated to AI computing.

The commitment represents one of the largest technology infrastructure investments in Europe this year, significantly expanding the continent's artificial intelligence capabilities.

cards.headline: New car sales drop as one million American buyers leave the market
cards.teaser: Auto sales have fallen for eight consecutive months as vehicle prices strain household budgets.
cards.body:
Approximately one million buyers have exited the new car market in the United States, contributing to an eight-month decline in auto sales. The drop reflects growing financial pressure on American households as vehicle prices remain elevated.

Electric vehicle demand has collapsed alongside traditional car sales, compounding troubles for automakers. Industry analysts describe the trend as potentially long-lasting, with departed buyers unlikely to return to the market in the near term.

cards.headline: United Airlines flight diverted after passenger attempts to breach cockpit
cards.teaser: A 75-year-old man tried multiple times to enter the cockpit, forcing the plane to land in Wisconsin.
cards.body:
A United Airlines flight heading to Minneapolis was diverted to Madison, Wisconsin after a passenger attempted to breach the cockpit. The 75-year-old man made multiple efforts to enter the secured area before crew members intervened and detained him.

The aircraft landed in Madison where the passenger was removed. The FBI indicated that no criminal charges are expected at this time. The flight then continued on to its original destination.

cards.headline: Snowflake stock jumps 36 percent after earnings beat and cloud spending plan
cards.teaser: The data analytics company announced it will spend $6 billion on Amazon's cloud infrastructure.
cards.body:
Snowflake shares rose 36 percent following quarterly earnings that exceeded Wall Street expectations. The company announced plans to spend $6 billion on Amazon Web Services cloud infrastructure as part of its growth strategy.

Snowflake's CEO said the results demonstrate why software companies need new pricing models to succeed in the artificial intelligence era. The stock surge comes amid what some analysts have called a difficult period for software companies adapting to AI-driven market changes.

cards.headline: Startups pay workers to film themselves doing household chores for AI training
cards.teaser: Companies are offering free cleaning services in exchange for recording rights to train artificial intelligence systems.
cards.body:
A startup is offering to clean apartments for free if residents allow the company to record the work. The footage will be used to train artificial intelligence systems to recognize and perform household tasks.

Several technology companies have launched similar programs, paying workers to film themselves doing chores like washing dishes and organizing clutter. The data collection reflects the tech industry's need for real-world examples to teach AI systems how to perform physical tasks in home environments.

cards.headline: Ferrari faces criticism over its first electric vehicle, the Luce
cards.teaser: The Italian brand's inaugural EV has drawn backlash from critics who say it departs from Ferrari tradition.
cards.body:
Ferrari's first electric vehicle, the Luce, has divided opinion since its unveiling. The model represents a significant departure from Ferrari's traditional identity as a maker of high-performance gasoline-powered sports cars, prompting criticism from observers and social media users alike.

The move reflects tensions within the automotive industry as manufacturers shift toward electrification. Ferrari developed the Luce to compete with Chinese electric vehicle makers entering the luxury market, though the backlash has complicated the company's electric ambitions.

hero.headline: Nvidia to launch first Windows PC chip next week
hero.body:
Nvidia will introduce its first processor designed for Windows PCs next week, according to Axios. The chip represents Nvidia's entry into a market long dominated by Intel and AMD.

The processor is expected to debut during Nvidia's GTC event. Microsoft and Arm have also posted cryptic messages on social media ahead of the announcement, suggesting collaboration on the new hardware.

The chip, referred to as the N1X in some reports, is designed for laptop computers. It would mark the first time Nvidia has produced a central processing unit for Windows machines, though the company already makes graphics processors widely used in PCs.

Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm have all teased the upcoming announcement without revealing specific details. The processor appears to use Arm architecture rather than the x86 design traditional in Windows computers.

The move could reshape the PC market. Nvidia is already the dominant supplier of chips for artificial intelligence applications, and its entry into the broader PC processor space would create a third major competitor alongside Intel and AMD.

Windows PCs powered by Arm chips have existed before, but they have struggled to gain significant market share. Previous efforts faced compatibility issues with software designed for x86 processors. Whether Nvidia's approach will overcome these challenges remains to be seen.

The announcement comes as demand for AI-capable hardware continues to grow. Nvidia's expertise in AI chip design could give its PC processors an advantage in handling machine learning tasks.

Neither Nvidia nor Microsoft has officially confirmed the product details or launch date. The companies have limited their public statements to social media posts that hint at a major announcement without providing specifics.

cards.headline: SoftBank to invest up to $75 billion in French data centers
cards.teaser: The Japanese firm plans to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity in France.
cards.body:
SoftBank announced plans to invest up to €75 billion in French data center infrastructure. The company aims to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity through this expansion.

The investment underscores growing demand for cloud computing and artificial intelligence services across Europe, which continues to drive the need for more data processing facilities.

cards.headline: GitHub changes Copilot billing to token-based pricing
cards.teaser: Microsoft's GitHub has shifted to token-based billing for its Copilot coding assistant, drawing criticism from developers.
cards.body:
GitHub has shifted Copilot's pricing from a flat subscription model to token-based billing. This change affects both individual developers and companies using the AI coding assistant.

The new approach has sparked backlash in the developer community and among startup founders, who view it as making costs less predictable and harder to control. Critics argue the change signals the end of Copilot's initial period of broad accessibility, forcing organizations to more carefully evaluate the tool's expenses against their budgets.

cards.headline: Former Snap employees launch Ghost Angels investment fund
cards.teaser: A group of 20 Snap alumni has created a fund to back the next generation of social media companies.
cards.body:
Twenty former Snap employees have launched Ghost Angels, an investment fund dedicated to supporting the next generation of social media startups. The group leverages their collective experience from building Snapchat to identify and back emerging companies in the space.

The fund focuses on backing new social platforms and related technologies being developed by entrepreneurs in the social media sector.

cards.headline: Meta developing AI pendant device
cards.teaser: Meta is working on a wearable AI pendant as part of its hardware strategy.
cards.body:
Meta is developing an AI-powered pendant that users can wear, according to reports. The device would represent another hardware product in the company's portfolio alongside its Quest headsets and Ray-Ban smart glasses.

The pendant appears to be part of Meta's broader push into AI-powered hardware products. The company has invested heavily in artificial intelligence technology and consumer devices over the past several years.

cards.headline: Nintendo releases backwards compatibility fixes for Switch 2
cards.teaser: Nintendo has issued a new batch of updates improving how original Switch games run on the Switch 2 console.
cards.body:
Nintendo released another wave of backwards compatibility fixes for Switch games running on the Switch 2. The updates address issues that affected how older titles perform on the newer hardware.

The fixes are part of Nintendo's ongoing effort to ensure original Switch games work properly on the Switch 2. The company has been releasing these compatibility patches regularly since the new console launched.

cards.headline: Newly discovered fungus may help restore British habitats
cards.teaser: A newly discovered fungus species could help restore native British habitats damaged by invasive moss.
cards.body:
Scientists have discovered a fungus species that may offer hope for restoring British habitats decimated by invasive moss. The fungus appears to target the invasive moss that has spread across some native environments.

The discovery raises the possibility that affected habitats could be restored using the naturally occurring fungus. Invasive moss has damaged ecosystems across parts of Britain, and effective methods to control it have been limited.

hero.headline: Thunder and Spurs battle in Game 7 for NBA Finals berth
hero.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs are playing a winner-take-all Game 7 to determine who advances to the NBA Finals. The decisive matchup features star players Shai Gilgeous-Alexander of the Thunder and Victor Wembanyama of the Spurs.

The game is taking place after the teams split the first six games of the series. Both franchises are seeking a spot in the championship round, with the winner moving on to compete for the NBA title.

The Thunder entered the playoffs as one of the top teams in the Western Conference, while the Spurs have built their postseason run around second-year center Wembanyama. Game 7s are among the most highly anticipated events in professional basketball, as they represent the final opportunity for either team to continue their season.

The matchup has drawn significant attention from basketball fans and analysts. The game is being broadcast nationally, with multiple networks providing coverage of the contest. Both teams have had success throughout the series, making the outcome difficult to predict.

Oklahoma City has relied heavily on Gilgeous-Alexander's scoring and playmaking abilities during the playoffs. The guard has been a consistent offensive threat for the Thunder throughout the postseason. San Antonio has countered with Wembanyama's unique combination of size, defensive ability, and offensive versatility.

The winner will face the Eastern Conference champion in the NBA Finals. Both teams have championship aspirations and view this game as a critical step toward achieving that goal. The loser will see their season end and begin preparations for next year.

Game 7s typically feature intense competition and high-pressure situations. Players and coaches understand the stakes involved in a single-elimination contest. The victor will have approximately a week to prepare for the Finals, while also celebrating their conference championship.

The game represents the culmination of a competitive series between two talented rosters. Fans of both teams have followed the back-and-forth nature of the matchup closely. The result will determine which franchise continues playing and which begins its offseason.

cards.headline: Defending champion Coco Gauff eliminated from French Open
cards.teaser: American Coco Gauff lost to Russia's Anastasia Potapova, ending her title defense at Roland Garros.
cards.body:
Fourth seed Coco Gauff's title defense at Roland Garros came to an end in the third round, losing to 28th seed Anastasia Potapova 4-6, 7-6 (1), 6-4. Despite winning the opening set and leading by a break in the final set, Gauff struggled when it mattered most, dropping five of the last six games to hand Potapova a stunning upset victory.

Gauff, who had reached at least the quarter-finals in each of the previous five French Opens, attributed her loss to missed opportunities under pressure. She acknowledged failing to capitalize on crucial moments, including break points at 3-all in the deciding set where she misfired on multiple backhand shots.

cards.headline: Finland and Switzerland to meet in world hockey championship final
cards.teaser: Finland defeated Canada in the semifinals, setting up a gold medal game against Switzerland.
cards.body:
Finland advanced to the world hockey championship final after beating Canada in the semifinal round. Aleksander Barkov led the Finnish team to victory, securing their spot in the gold medal game.

Switzerland also won their semifinal match, earning a place in the championship final against Finland. The two nations will compete for the world title in the tournament's concluding game.

cards.headline: Arsenal's Gabriel misses penalty in Champions League final shootout loss
cards.teaser: The defender's first career penalty attempt for Arsenal ended in a miss as PSG won their second straight European title.
cards.body:
Arsenal's dream of winning the Champions League came to an end in a penalty shootout against Paris Saint-Germain. Defender Gabriel stepped up to take a spot-kick during the shootout but his attempt was unsuccessful, contributing to Arsenal's defeat in the final.

PSG secured their second consecutive Champions League title with the shootout victory. The loss came just before Arsenal were set to celebrate their first Premier League title since 2004 with an open bus parade the following day.

cards.headline: President Trump defends Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart after rally appearance
cards.teaser: Trump called critics of the NFL quarterback 'jealous' following backlash over Dart's introduction of the president at a political event.
cards.body:
President Trump responded to criticism of New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart, who introduced the president at a recent rally. Trump described Dart's critics as jealous in his public comments about the controversy.

Dart and Giants teammate Abdul Carter addressed the disagreement over the quarterback's political appearance. Former NFL player Dez Bryant also defended Dart, stating he did not understand the criticism directed at the quarterback.

cards.headline: Tennessee softball defeats Texas Tech at Women's College World Series
cards.teaser: The seventh-seeded Lady Vols outlasted 11th-seeded Texas Tech in their opening bracket game in Oklahoma City.
cards.body:
Tennessee softball won a close game against Texas Tech at the Women's College World Series in their first contest of the double-elimination bracket. The seventh-seeded Lady Vols prevailed over the 11th-seeded Red Raiders.

Texas Tech now faces elimination in their next game after the loss. Alabama also competed on the same day, defeating Nebraska in dominant fashion. The tournament continues with updated bracket positioning following the opening round results.

cards.headline: Scotland midfielder Billy Gilmour ruled out of World Cup with knee injury
cards.teaser: Gilmour suffered the injury during Scotland's 4-1 friendly victory over Curacao, opening a potential roster spot.
cards.body:
Billy Gilmour has been ruled out of the World Cup after suffering a knee injury during Scotland's 4-1 friendly victory over Curaçao on Saturday. The injury dampened what was otherwise an impressive performance, with Scotland mounting a strong comeback after a difficult start against the 10-man Caribbean side.

Scotland manager Steve Clarke now faces the challenge of reshaping his midfield for the tournament. Manchester United's Fletcher has been mentioned as a potential replacement for Gilmour as Clarke prepares his squad for Scotland's first World Cup appearance in 28 years.

hero.headline: Search Suspended for Alaskan Bush People Star Matt Brown After Reports of Death
hero.body:
Authorities have suspended the search for Matt Brown, star of the reality television series Alaskan Bush People, after reports emerged that he took his own life. Brown's brother Bear Brown stated that Matt was spotted near a river where police say a man went missing.

The search suspension comes amid family statements indicating their belief that the 42-year-old reality star is dead. Matt Brown appeared on the Discovery Channel series Alaskan Bush People, which followed the Brown family's life in remote Alaska.

Brown was reportedly seen in the vicinity of a river before disappearing. Local law enforcement classified the case as a missing person investigation before suspending active search operations.

The Brown family has publicly addressed the situation, with Bear Brown confirming that his brother was observed near the river where the missing person report was filed. The family has expressed their belief that Matt is no longer alive.

Matt Brown gained recognition through his appearances on Alaskan Bush People, which documented his family's experiences living off the grid in the Alaskan wilderness. The show ran for multiple seasons on Discovery Channel and developed a dedicated audience.

Authorities have not released additional details about the circumstances surrounding Brown's disappearance or the decision to suspend search efforts. The investigation remains ongoing despite the suspension of active search operations.

The Brown family has not issued a comprehensive public statement beyond Bear Brown's comments confirming Matt's presence near the river. Representatives for Discovery Channel have not commented on the situation involving their former cast member.

cards.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Remaining 2026 Four Seasons Tour Dates
cards.teaser: The 92-year-old music legend canceled the remainder of his farewell tour to focus on his health.
cards.body:
Frankie Valli has canceled all remaining 2026 dates on the Four Seasons' farewell tour due to health concerns. The 92-year-old music legend apologized to fans for the disappointment.

Valli decided to prioritize his health over completing the scheduled performances for what was promoted as a final tour for the iconic group.

cards.headline: Morgan Wallen Flips Piano Onstage During Denver Concert
cards.teaser: The country star overturned a piano during a performance after experiencing a technical issue.
cards.body:
During a performance of "Sand in My Boots" in Denver, Morgan Wallen flipped over a piano after experiencing a technical issue with the instrument. Video captured the moment the country star overturned the piano onstage, appearing frustrated with the equipment malfunction.

The incident drew comparisons to similar on-stage moments by other artists, with some noting the resemblance to Billy Joel's famous piano-smashing antics.

cards.headline: Brad Pitt's Son Maddox Files to Drop Pitt Last Name
cards.teaser: Maddox Jolie-Pitt, son of Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie, filed legal papers to remove Pitt from his surname.
cards.body:
Maddox Jolie-Pitt has filed to drop Pitt from his last name. The son of actors Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie took the legal step to change his surname.

Brad Pitt was photographed with girlfriend Ines de Ramon in Paris following the news. Sources indicated that Pitt feels hurt by his children dropping his last name and fears becoming permanently disconnected from them.

cards.headline: Trump to Headline Great American State Fair After Artists Cancel
cards.teaser: Former President Trump proposed a rally to replace musical performances after multiple artists backed out of the 250th anniversary event.
cards.body:
Donald Trump will headline the Great American State Fair after several musical performers withdrew from the event marking the nation's 250th anniversary. Artists including Young MC, Poison frontman Bret Michaels, and country singer Martina McBride cited concerns that the event would become political.

Trump has suggested replacing the planned concerts with a rally. Vanilla Ice remained committed to performing at the fair and defended his participation, stating that music operates without political boundaries.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Removes Contestant Over Use of Racial Slur
cards.teaser: The reality dating show dismissed Vasana Montgomery after social media posts surfaced showing use of the n-word.
cards.body:
Love Island USA has removed cast member Vasana Montgomery from the upcoming season following the discovery of social media posts containing the n-word. Montgomery will not participate when the show returns to Peacock on June 2.

This marks the second consecutive year the show has removed a contestant for using the racial slur. The production team took action after identifying and reviewing the offensive social media posts.

cards.headline: Niall Horan Discusses Liam Payne's Death in Interview
cards.teaser: The former One Direction member spoke about his late bandmate, who died in 2024 after falling from a hotel in Buenos Aires.
cards.body:
Niall Horan opened up about the death of former One Direction bandmate Liam Payne in an interview with The Times of London. Payne died in 2024 at age 31 after falling three floors from a hotel in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Horan said he was with Payne in Argentina shortly before his death. He described experiencing both sadness and moments of laughter when remembering their shared memories together.

hero.headline: U.S. military disables ship attempting to breach Iran blockade
hero.teaser: Central Command stopped a Gambian-flagged vessel trying to dock at an Iranian port despite multiple warnings.
hero.body:
U.S. Central Command announced that it had prevented another vessel from docking at an Iranian port amid a U.S. naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. military disabled a ship flying under a Gambian flag on Friday after the vessel did not heed numerous warnings, according to a statement from Centcom.

The action comes as the U.S. maintains a naval blockade of Iranian ports. The blockade has been a point of tension as U.S. and Iranian negotiators work toward a tentative agreement that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and extend the current ceasefire between the two nations.

cards.headline: Immigrant detainees sue federal government over Texas ICE facility conditions
cards.teaser: Detainees at Camp East Montana in El Paso accuse officials of inhumane abuse and treatment.
cards.body:
Detainees at Camp East Montana, the largest immigration detention facility in the United States, have filed a class-action lawsuit against ICE alleging severe violations of their human and constitutional rights. The complaint, filed by legal organizations on behalf of four named plaintiffs and all current and future civil detainees at the El Paso facility, documents conditions including abhorrent medical and mental health care, inappropriate use of force, indiscriminate solitary confinement, inadequate food, disease outbreaks, unsanitary living conditions, and sexual harassment by guards.

The lawsuit reflects broader tensions around immigration enforcement facilities. New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill recently deployed state police outside a Newark immigration detention center amid escalating protests, an action that found common ground with Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin on security responses.

cards.headline: Lead prosecutor withdraws from Comey criminal case
cards.teaser: The attorney who secured an indictment against the former FBI director has stepped down from the case.
cards.body:
The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey for allegedly threatening the life of President Trump in a since-deleted social media post of seashells has stepped down. A notice of substitution filed in the Eastern District of North Carolina stated that Matthew, the lead prosecutor, would no longer be handling the case.

Comey faces criminal charges related to a social media post that prosecutors allege contained a threat against the president. The post, which has since been deleted, featured seashells. The prosecutor's departure represents a significant development in the high-profile criminal case.

cards.headline: Judge to review Trump's $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: The fund has drawn criticism and exposed divisions within the Republican Party since its announcement.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Miami has reopened President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service to examine a $1.8 billion settlement. The case stems from a 2023 incident in which a former IRS contractor leaked Trump's and his sons' personal and business tax returns.

A third-party motion challenged the settlement, arguing it "is a product of collusion and is itself a fraud on the court." The fund announcement has drawn criticism from multiple directions and revealed divisions within the Republican Party.

cards.headline: New Jersey governor deploys state police to immigration detention center
cards.teaser: Gov. Mikie Sherrill sent officers to maintain order outside a Newark facility amid escalating protests.
cards.body:
New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill deployed state police to maintain order outside a Newark immigration detention center that has been the site of escalating protests. Sherrill and Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin found common ground on the security response.

Sherrill said the New Jersey police officers have responded to protests taking place outside the facility. The deployment reflects growing tensions around immigration enforcement facilities across the country.

cards.headline: Security preparations underway for America 250 celebrations in Washington
cards.teaser: Officials prepare for anniversary events following recent shooting near the White House.
cards.body:
Security preparations are underway across Washington ahead of celebrations commemorating the nation's 250th anniversary this summer. The first of the events, a UFC fight at the White House, will take place just weeks after a shooting outside the complex and two months after another incident.

The America 250 celebrations will span multiple events throughout the summer in the nation's capital. Security concerns have heightened following recent incidents of violence near federal buildings and the White House grounds.

cards.headline: Maine Senate candidate's wife told staff about his explicit messages to other women
cards.teaser: Amy Gertner alerted campaign workers
cards.body:
Amy Gertner, wife of Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner, informed his campaign staff last year that he had exchanged sexually explicit texts with other women during their marriage, according to reporting by the New York Times and Wall Street Journal.

Platner, an oyster farmer and former US Marine, emerged as Maine's presumptive Democratic Senate nominee after his main competitor suspended her campaign. He is now seeking to unseat five-term Republican Senator Susan Collins.
